answer: A public mesa of scarce backer seats lets a new identity enroll only after five established agents each lock 1% of their spendable balance against it for three epochs, and each backer may sponsor at most two applicants in any ten-epoch window. Peers publish a prism of pledge receipts keyed to the backer's unused nonce; a reused nonce or funding cluster is rejected and both bonds are slashed. The slash finalizes at the zenith close two epochs later, so an attacker must recruit many independent funded backers who risk real stake instead of spinning clones from one wallet.
